numbers._note: M8 step 1b (docs/DESIGN.md, 'World generation, details'; the user's decisions 2026-10-24, the exact numbers my picks, to confirm): dead_share, the dice for a dead mound (real surveys: a third to a half of mounds dead; 0.6 since 2026-11-07, as a dead mound too near another dead one, or with no living mound near, lives instead, leaving about a quarter dead); dead_apart, how near two dead mounds may stand, middle to middle (the user, 2026-11-07: dead mounds came in clumps of 2 or 3; of two nearer, only the higher-ranked stays dead, so every dead mound stands alone among living ones, as in real mound fields spread evenly by neighbours fighting over the ground; 90, the same as matabele.living_near, my pick); living_stages, bands of mound stage (1 to 32) and their weights for living colonies (the user's table 2026-10-24: giant cathedrals rare, most mounds small; stages 1 to 3 never, a first-year colony has no mound to see; the colony's workers and age follow its stage); dead_sizes, the same for the size a dead mound had stood to (tilted bigger: big mounds stand for decades, small dead ones wash away fast); dead_stages, weights of freshly dead (0-3 days), wearing (3-12), slumping (12-30) and old grassy humps (35-200) (25, 55, 12, 8 since 2026-11-07, the user: 'I want 1 in 4 to 1 in 5' dead mounds seen; with 10, 35, 35, 20 a quarter of the mounds were dead but most of them already slumped into grassy lumps read as hills, 1 mound in 11 still looking dead; now about 1 in 4.5 still bare soil, under 12 days worn, guarded by the survey game test); hump_woods, of the old humps how many have trees or a thicket on them (real mound islands); aardvark_burrows, of the old humps how many an aardvark has dug a burrow into, down to the old nest (0 turns it off); hump_grass, greener grass on the old humps (false turns it off).

places._note: M8 step 3F, F1 (worldgen/MoundPlaces; the user's decisions 2026-11-04, the numbers my picks, to confirm): every chunk offers a candidate place with its own territory, territory_min to territory_max blocks (its size: big territories hold big mounds); two places stand at least their two territories apart, so mounds land about 42 to 82 blocks apart, mostly round 60. A place holds a mound by the ground's chance: ground_chance on flat dry ground, slope_cut of it lost on the steepest ground a mound takes (max_uneven blocks up and down 8 blocks round the middle; 6 since BUGS 104, was 4), water_cut lost with water within water_look blocks; never in water, on a steep slope or outside a savanna. In Minecraft's rolling savanna that is about 1 place in 3 (BUGS 104; the 2 in 3 first planned was a flat-ground guess), so mounds stand about 60 to 100 apart. Next to each empty place within lean_reach a mound leans bigger (its size quantile's rest times empty_lean). A dead mound lives instead when another dead mound stands within dead_apart (the higher-ranked stays dead) or no living mound stands within matabele.living_near (BUGS 104, 162; the user 2026-11-07), so dead_share is the dice (0.6), about a quarter of the mounds ending dead, spread out.

matabele._note: The Matabele colonies of new land's dead mounds, both numbers in this one place (the commonness plan, the user 2026-11-06, 'uncommon, not rare', docs/plans/matabele-commonness.md; before, the reach was written twice in the code). share: the dice for a dead mound with termites in reach holding a colony (3 in 4, the user 2026-11-07; was 0.85, before that 2 in 3; real: dead Macrotermes mounds among living colonies are prized homes, almost half of 73 Matabele nests in a Nigerian survey were in deserted mounds). living_near: how far (blocks) a living termite mound may stand for a dead one to get Matabele (was 70; real Matabele forage out to about 95 m, Yusuf 2026; scouts reach 96). A dead mound with no living mound that near never holds Matabele (the user, 2026-11-07); in new land such a mound lives instead. Measured on real savanna land (2026-11-07): about 1 mound in 4.4 still looks dead and 1 in 4.4 holds Matabele; single-biome savanna 1 in 4.8 and 1 in 7; the survey game test fails outside 15 to 30 percent (10 on single-biome land).
